ut

conjunction, with the indicative; often answered by ita or sīc · Wiktionary

The plain “as”, in comparisons and in asides: ut ajunt, as they say; ut soleō, as usual; ut libet, as you like.

Other words

  • sīcut (sīcutī) — just as

    conjunction, with the indicative; answered by ita or sīc · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 5.14.1: sīcut soleō; Traupman 273 · Wiktionary

    A stronger ut: “exactly as”.

  • quemadmodum — in the way that, as

    relative adverb, with the indicative; answered by sīc or ita · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 47.11: sīc cum īnferiōre vīvās quemadmodum tēcum superiōrem velīs vīvere · Wiktionary

    “In what way”: also the question “how?” and, in an indirect question, with the subjunctive (quaeris quemadmodum … diem dispōnam, Plin. Ep. 9.36.1).

Examples

  • persevērā ut coepistī

    keep on as you have begunSen. Ep. 4.1

  • Age age, ut libet.

    All right, all right, as you like.Ter. And. 310

  • ut ajunt, deī facientēs adjuvant

    as they say, the gods help those who get on with itVarr. RR 1.1.4

  • S. V. B. E. V., sīcut soleō, paululō tamen etiam dēterius quam soleō

    if you are well, good; I am well, as usual, though a little worse even than usualCic. Fam. 5.14.1

  • sīc cum īnferiōre vīvās quemadmodum tēcum superiōrem velīs vīvere

    live with those below you as you would want those above you to live with youSen. Ep. 47.11

See also as if, as … as, thus, as usual.
